problems.title: Maximum rectangle area
problems.question: A rectangle has three-side sum 30m. Find its maximum are a.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
formulas: Let repeated side be x and the other 30−2x. A=x(30−2x)=112.5−2(x−7.5)².
steps: The maximum 112.5 occurs for sides 7.5 and 15.

problems.title: A logarithmic definite integral
problems.question: Evaluate∫₀^(e/2) dx/(e−x).
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
steps: The value is −ln(e/2)+ln e=ln2.

problems.title: An antiderivative of tangent squared
problems.question: Find an antiderivative of tan²x.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
steps: Integrating gives tanx−x+C, on any interval where tangent is defined.

problems.title: Plane from a point and normal
problems.question: Write the plane through(1,2,2) normal to(2,−3,−1).
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
steps: Expand to 2x−3y−z+6=0.

problems.title: Translate an ellipse
problems.question: An ellipse has vertices(±3,0),(0,±2). Translate it by(−2,3).
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
formulas: The original equation is x²/9+y²/4=1. Replace x by x+2 and y by y−3.
steps: Multiply the translated equation by 36.

problems.title: Inflection points of a polynomial times an exponential
problems.question: How many inflection points has f=x³eˣ?
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
steps: The three roots are 0,−3±√3. Each is simple, so f″ changes sign at all three.

problems.title: Area between reciprocal curves
problems.question: Find the are a where y>x² and y<√x.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
formulas: The curves meet at x=0,1; are a=∫₀¹(√x−x²)dx.
steps: Evaluate[2x^(3/2)/3−x³/3]₀¹=1/3.

problems.title: A washer volume
problems.question: Rotate the region between y=√7·x³/√π, y=√5·x²/√π, x=1, x=2 about the x-axis.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
formulas: The first curve is above the second. Washer are a is π(y₁²−y₂²)=7x⁶−5x⁴.
steps: Volume=∫₁²(7x⁶−5x⁴)dx=[x⁷−x⁵]₁²=128−32=96.

problems.title: A hyperbola’s vertex separation
problems.question: A standard centred hyperbola has asymptote y=0.75x and focus(−5,0). Find its vertex distance.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
steps: The 3:4:5 relation gives a=4, b=3. Vertex separation is 2a=8.
problems.note: The usual standard hyperbola centred at the origin with coordinate-axis principal axes is intended.

problems.title: Parabola from focus and directrix
problems.question: Find the parabola with focus(−2,1), directrix x=4.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
steps: Expand and cancel x² to get y²−2y+12x−11=0.

problems.title: A globally increasing function
problems.question: Where is f(x)=2x−sinx increasing?
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
steps: The derivative is positive for every real x, so f is strictly increasing on all of R.

problems.title: Incircle of a coordinate triangle
problems.question: Find the incircle of vertices(0,0),(6,0),(0,8).
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
steps: The centre is(2,2). Thus(x−2)²+(y−2)²=4, or x²+y²=4(x+y−1).

problems.question: Evaluate∫₀^π x sinx dx.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.

problems.title: Intercept of an oblique asymptote
problems.question: Where does the oblique asymptote of y=2x+2+1/x meet the y-axis?
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
formulas: The difference from y=2x+2 is 1/x→0 as|x|→∞.
steps: Thus the asymptote is y=2x+2, and its intercept is(0,2).

problems.title: Largest cyclic trapezoid with diameter base
problems.question: A trapezoid has one base a circle diameter and all vertices on the circle. Radius R=⁴√3. Find maximum are a.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
formulas: Let half the other base be u,0≤u<R. Height=√(R²−u²), are a A=(R+u)√(R²−u²).
steps: Differentiate A²=(R+u)³(R−u). Its interior maximum has 3/(R+u)=1/(R−u), so u=R/2.
Maximum A=3√3R²/4=9/4 since R²=√3.

problems.title: Circle through two ellipses’ intersections
problems.question: Find the circumcircle diameter of the intersections of x²/25+y²/16=1 and x²/16+y²/25=1.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
formulas: Subtraction gives x²=y². Substitution gives x²=y²=400/41.
steps: All four intersections have radius √(800/41). Diameter=40√82/41.

problems.title: Count intersections of two ellipses
problems.question: Count roots of 9(x−1)²+4(y−1)²=36 and 4(x−4)²+9(y−2)²=36.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
formulas: Any intersection has 1≤x≤3. On this interval, the first ellipse’s upper arc decreases from 4 to 1; the second upper arc increases from 2 to 2+4√2/3.
steps: The upper arcs cross exactly once, by strict opposite monotonicity and their endpoint values. The lower arcs also cross exactly once for the same reason.

Crossed arc pairs cannot meet:the first lower arc is at most1 while the second upper arc is at least2. For the other pair, when1≤x≤2 the first upper arc exceeds3 and the second lower arc is at most2; when2≤x≤3, the first upper arc is at least1 while the second lower arc is at most2−2√5/3<1.

problems.title: Three planes meet at one point
problems.question: Find the distance from 0 to the common point of x−y+5z=0,2x+3y+7z=10 and z=0.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
formulas: With z=0, the first gives x=y and the second5x=10.
steps: The point is(2,2,0), distance√8.

problems.title: Least surface area at fixed cylinder volume
problems.question: A cylinder has volume2π. Find the height that minimizes total surface are a.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
steps: S′=4πr−4π/r²=0 gives r³=1, r=1, h=2. The surface tends to∞ at both radius extremes, so this is the global minimum.

problems.title: Minimum reciprocal sum
problems.question: Find the minimum of 1/(x−1)+1/(2−x) for 1<x<2.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
formulas: Let u=x−1, v=2−x; u, v>0 and u+v=1. Then1/u+1/v=1/(uv).
steps: Since uv≤1/4, the sum is≥4. Equality occurs at u=v=1/2, or x=1.5.

problems.title: Probability under a hyperbola
problems.question: Independent uniform X, Y lie in[0, e]. Find P(XY≤1).
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
formulas: The square are a is e². Favourable are a=∫₀^(1/e)e dx+∫_(1/e)^e dx/x.
steps: It equals 1+[lnx]_(1/e)^e=1+2=3. Divide by e².
problems.note: This uses the usual independent-selection interpretation. Uniform marginal distributions alone, without independence, would not determine this probability.

problems.title: Right-triangle area under a sum condition
problems.question: A right triangle’s hypotenuse c plus altitude h to it equals 30. Find maximum are a.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
formulas: h≤c/2, so with c=30−h we have 0<h≤10. Area A=ch/2=h(30−h)/2.
steps: This increases on0<h≤10. The maximum occurs at h=10, c=20, an isosceles right triangle. A=100.

problems.title: Count quintic roots with derivative signs
problems.question: Count real roots of x⁵/5−13x³/3+36x+1=0.
problems.idea: Set up the standard coordinate, derivative, or integral formula and simplify.
steps: The two negative critical values are negative:f(−3)=−38.6, f(−2)=−42.733… . Both positive critical values are positive:f(2)=44.733…, f(3)=40.6.
The function increases from f(−2)<0 to f(2)>0 on(−2,2), so has exactly one root there. Its outer extrema signs exclude every other root.
